caption: Find cells a road cannot pass through.
content:
Especially early in the game, when you have only a few road tiles, the possible shapes of your roads are limited.
If you're having trouble connecting a road, @b{mark cells that the road cannot pass through with @m{unsatisfied}} to narrow down the possible routes.

content.caption: Example
content: Suppose your available tiles are @t{forest_road.2s.lr} @t{forest_road.2t.dr} @t{forest_road.2t.ul} @t{forest_road.2t.ur}. In the Area below, our goal is to reach the road on the right.

First, look at the cell @m{pending}. You don't have any tiles that can be placed on this cell.
Therefore, the road cannot pass through the cell @m{pending}. Let's mark cells like this with @m{unsatisfied}.
Next, look at the cell @m{pending}. The only tiles that can be placed on this cell are @t{forest_road.2s.lr} and @t{forest_road.2t.dr}.

However, whichever tile you place, the road would have to enter the cell @m{unsatisfied} on the right.
Therefore, the road cannot pass through the cell @m{pending} either.

Now we can see that, to keep the road from passing through the cells @m{unsatisfied}, it must be extended as shown below.
@b{By identifying the cells @m{unsatisfied} that the road cannot pass through, we were able to narrow down the possible route.}
From here, simply extend the road straight ahead to connect it as shown.
